Getting started

A tour of the window and where everything lives.

#A tour of Doceo

The left bar is your library, the top bar holds your open tabs, and the main area shows the page you are on.

  1. Quick links on the left jump between Dashboard, All notes, Calendar, Tasks, Files, Whiteboards, Databases (when switched on) and Insights.
  2. Folders sit below the quick links as a real tree. Drag a page or folder onto another folder to move it.
  3. Search (Ctrl+K) finds pages, folders and app pages; Recent (Ctrl+R) shows what you opened lately.
  4. The ••• menu at the top right changes with what you are looking at: a page, a folder, or an app page.

Tip Collapse the left bar with the button beside the window controls for a distraction-free Focus mode.

#The Get started checklist

The Dashboard lists a few things worth trying; each line does the thing and ticks itself off.

  1. Click a line to do it (write a note, add a task, open the daily note, try the command bar, look at the calendar, import, choose a look).
  2. Hide it when you’re done; ••• is not needed — press Ctrl+Shift+P and choose “Show the Get started checklist again” to bring it back.

#The bell: what needs attention

The bell in the top bar gathers what is overdue, due today, starting soon, due for review or ending.

  1. Click the bell for the list: overdue and due-today tasks, meetings starting within three hours, reminders, pages due for review, a sprint about to end, and tasks blocked by others.
  2. Click an item to go straight to it. The red number counts the urgent ones.

#The command bar

Ctrl+Shift+P: type what you want to do instead of hunting for it.

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+P (or type > at the start of the search box) and start typing: “new task”, “go to calendar”, “theme”, “archive”…
  2. Use ↑ ↓ and Enter. Recently used commands are listed first when the box is empty.
  3. While a page is open the bar also offers actions for that page: properties, versions, reminder, move, duplicate, archive, favourite…

Tip Anything you can do from a menu can be reached from the command bar — if you can’t find a feature, type a word for it here.

#Where your data lives

Everything is stored on your computer as plain files — nothing is uploaded.

  1. Open Settings → Your files to see the folder and open it.
  2. Notes, folders, tasks, calendars, databases and whiteboards are small JSON files; documents you edit in Page view are saved as .docx files.
  3. To back up or move to another computer, copy that folder and put it back in the same place.

#Themes and appearance

Pick a light, dark or coloured theme.

  1. Open ••• → Themes, or Settings → Appearance.
  2. Choose a theme; it applies everywhere without moving anything.

#Make Doceo easier to read and use

Larger text, higher contrast, a simpler screen, a readable font and bigger buttons.

  1. Open Settings → Accessibility.
  2. Text size makes the sidebar, tabs and pages larger (Standard, Large, Larger, Largest). Documents keep their own zoom.
  3. Contrast darkens secondary text and firms up lines. Simple view hides shortcut hints, tips and decoration.
  4. Readable font and Line spacing make text easier to follow; Buttons and rows makes targets bigger; Focus outline makes the keyboard position unmistakable; Motion → Reduced stops animations (your system’s Reduce motion setting is also honoured).
  5. Autosave is always on: notes, pages, slides and sheets save a moment after you stop typing.

#Trash: restore or empty

Deleted notes wait in the Trash until you restore them or empty it.

  1. Open Trash from the sidebar (the bin icon). Click a note to preview it; Restore brings it back, the bin button deletes it for good.
  2. Right-click Trash in the sidebar → Open trash, Restore all notes or Empty trash.
  3. The round button at the bottom right empties the whole trash after you confirm — it can’t be undone.

#Tabs and breadcrumbs

Open several pages at once and jump between them.

  1. Click a page to open it in a tab; the + asks which kind to make (Note, Page, Slides or Sheet, or a template). Right-click a tab to open it beside the current one (split view).
  2. Drag a tab to reorder it, or pull it out of the strip to open it in its own window; drop it back on the strip to dock it again.
  3. Ctrl+W closes a tab. Alt+← / Alt+→ moves the focused tab.
  4. Settings → Tabs & navigation puts the breadcrumbs under the tabs or in the top bar.
